topic.title: References Tab
topic.shortdesc: Use the References tab of the Explore side view to see the files that reference a file, and the files that it references.

body.p: The References tab (found in the Explore side view of the Personal Workspace) shows one file at a time, with the references between it and the other files of the project as a tree. For how the tab finds the references, see .

fig.title: The References Tab Showing the Topics That Reuse a Warning

p.note: The tab is experimental, and it is off by default. To turn it on, open your Profile page and, in the Preferences section, select Show the DITA References tab in the Explore side view. The tab is available in projects that define publications.

section.title: Opening the Tab
section.p: You can open the tab from these places:

dlentry.dd: Click the References tab icon. The tab starts on the root map of the active publication.
Choose Show references from the menu of a file.
Right-click inside an element and choose Show References. The tab highlights the references to the element at the caret, or to its closest ancestor that has an ID.
Choose Show References from the context menu of an element in the tree editor.

section.p: Each of these shows the file in the Referenced by direction.

dlentry.dd: Move through the files that you showed in the tab.
Reads the files of the workspace again. The tab does not follow your edits, so click it after you change files.
Opens the shown file in the editor. When the shown file is a web address, the button is Open URL and opens the address in a new browser tab.

dlentry.dt: Use the context publication as scope
dlentry.dd: Limits the tab to the files that the context publication includes. The tab then resolves keys and applies profiling as the publication does. Click it again to return to the whole project. The browser remembers your choice.

section.title: Choosing a File
section.p: The field under the toolbar names the shown file. To show another file, click the field and type part of a file name or a path. Separate several words with spaces: a file has to match all of them. Files whose names start with the text come first, then files whose names or paths contain it. With nothing typed, the list shows the most referenced files first.

Each file in the list shows how many references it has, for example 3 in · 2 out. The tabs above the list filter it by kind, and show how many files of each kind there are: All, Keys, Topics, Aliases, Maps, Resources, URLs, DITAVAL, and Problems. A tab appears only when the project has files of its kind. Problems lists the files that are referenced but do not exist or cannot be read, and the keys that no map defines.

section.title: Direction
section.p: The two buttons under the field choose what the tree shows:

ul.li: Referenced by - The files that reference the shown file.
References - The files that the shown file references.

section.p: A file that only the project file references, such as a root map, starts on References. Every other file starts on Referenced by.

section.title: Reading the Tree
section.p: Each node of the tree is a file, a key or a web address. Expand a node to see the next level in the same direction. Hover over a node to see the full path.

ul.li: Files show the icon of their type. Keys and aliases show a key icon, and web addresses a link icon.
A red error icon marks a file that does not exist or that cannot be read.
[def] marks the map nodes that define a key. They come first.
[alias] marks a copy of a topic made with the copy-to attribute.
[source] is the opposite relation of the [alias].
When other files reference two or more elements of the shown file, the Referenced by nodes are grouped by element, under Element id="..." or Root element.
A loop icon marks a file that is already shown above in the same branch of the tree. The node does not expand, so the tree cannot run in circles.

section.p: The nodes are sorted by kind: keys, topics, aliases, maps, resources, web addresses, DITAVAL files, then the missing and unreadable files. Nodes of the same kind keep the order of the references in the document.

section.title: Several References Between Two Files
section.p: When a file references another one more than once, e.g. , the node shows the number of references. Click the number to list them. Each reference shows its kind, and the tooltip says on which line of which file it is.

dlentry.dd: Opens the referencing file in the editor, with the caret in the element that holds the reference. A node that has no reference opens its file. A file that the editor cannot open becomes the shown file instead. Clicking an element group opens the shown file at that element.
Available in the menu of a node. Opens the file in the editor, or the web address in a new browser tab.
Available in the menu of a node. Shows that file in the tab. Use Back to return.
